To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the genetic architecture of the 2 ecotypes of M. guttatus includes both additive and epistatic interactions, 2) the magnitude of effect of alleles at the QTL was dependent on the background genotype, 3) the genetic architecture was different for the 2 ecotype QTL, 4) the genetic architecture is complex, and 5) the genetic architecture differs from that observed in previous studies.

(1) the 2 chromosomal regions that we examined are associated with many life history trait differences between populations, (2) these 2 chromosomal loci interact in a complex manner, and (3) the effects of alleles are stronger in the perennial genetic background.
the 2 chromosomal regions we have studied contain genetic variants that affect life history traits, and that the genetic effects are often different in the 2 genetic backgrounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the genetic basis of population differences in life-history traits.
the genetic architecture of life history traits in Mimulus guttatus, an annual/perennial pair of closely related ecotypes.
the genetic and epigenetic basis of complex traits in natural populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genetic basis of life history trait differences is complex, involving both main and epistatic effects of QTL, and that the genetic architecture of these traits may be influenced by genetic background.

epistatic interactions among the loci controlling life history traits are common in M. guttat us and that these interactions are likely to be an important component of adaptive divergence between populations.
epistatic interactions are important in determining phenotypic variation in natural populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DIV1 and, to a lesser extent, the DIV2 QTLS are important genetic components of life history divergence between the annual and perennial ecotype.
life history trait differences between M. guttatus ecotypes are due to the additive and interactive effects of multiple QTL.
epistatic interactions are important for understanding population divergence in this system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic architecture underlying life history divergence in M. Guttatus is complex, with both main effects and interactions between QTL.
epistasis can play an important role in the genetic architecture of complex traits and that epistasis is not simply a function of genetic background.
genetic background strongly influences the magnitude of QTL effects and that epistasis is an important factor in shaping the evolution of complex traits.
